_comment: Where each voter-requirement field comes from, and what could not be
obtained. This lives in its own file because provenance is the whole
point of the dataset: a reader turned away from a polling place needs to
know which source told us what, and when it was checked.
NCSL (ncsl.org) is the canonical source for the voter-ID STRICTNESS
taxonomy (strict-photo / photo-requested / non-photo / no-ID) and for the
same-day-registration and early-voting comparison tables. It returns 403
to automated clients on every one of those four tables, verified
2026-09-21. That classification is therefore ABSENT from this dataset
rather than reconstructed: deriving 'strict photo ID' from a paragraph of
prose is exactly the flattening that sends someone to the polls with the
Google Civic voterinfo (electionId 12000, the live 2026 General Midterm)
returns a state block containing only a name and a VIP source stub - no
electionAdministrationBody, no URLs. Verified for TX; MA and WI fail
address parsing outright. It contributes nothing here yet.

vote.org/voter-id-laws.shape: 52-row table: State | In-Person Voter ID Laws | Absentee Voter ID Laws

vote.org/voter-registration-deadlines.shape: 52-row table: State | Voter Registration Deadlines | Election Day Registration

vote.org/early-voting-calendar.shape: 52-row table: State | begins | ends | More Information

vote.org/absentee-ballot-deadlines.shape: 52-row table: State | Application Deadline | Ballot Due | Ballot Tracker

vote.org/absentee-voting-rules.shape: prose sections delimited by '<State> absentee ballot rules' headings

unavailable.ncsl_voter_id_strictness: 403 to automated clients; classification omitted rather than inferred
unavailable.polling_hours: no free per-state structured source found; state election office governs
unavailable.google_civic_admin_body: state block carries name + VIP stub only, no URLs
